headline: High: slim can write and egress broadly, creating default data-leak and action-conflict risk; awesome-selfhosted is read-only but can still be misused as an untrusted content source.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a read-only knowledge-management source with no execution surface, while slim is an interactive CLI that reads files and stdout/stderr. There is no documented shared channel, so prompt injection is only plausible via manual copy/paste or if slim ingests untrusted text from the list. That makes the pathway possible but narrow.
conditions: IF an operator copies content from awesome-selfhosted into slim's interactive prompt as instructions
IF slim is configured to parse repository text from the knowledge list as commands
mitigations: Treat awesome-selfhosted content as untrusted text only
Use a separate review step before pasting into slim
Disable any automation that feeds list content into CLI prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for copied snippets

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted itself has no data classes touched and no egress, but slim touches filesystem artifacts, environment variables, certificate private keys, and has broad network egress. If both are used in the same workspace, slim can read and transmit sensitive local files while the list source provides untrusted operational guidance. The pair creates a default leakage path through the writable/readable filesystem.
conditions: IF slim is run in a workspace containing secrets, keys, or environment files
IF outputs from awesome-selfhosted are used to select or configure slim against that workspace
mitigations: Run slim in a clean temporary directory
Remove secrets and key files from the target workspace
Restrict outbound network during analysis
Review any copied instructions from awesome-selfhosted before execution
requires-engineering: isolate slim with a dedicated sandbox and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write capabilities, but slim can write the filesystem and execute shells. Even without modify_git_state, overlapping writes to the same directory can still clobber artifacts or generated files if the list is used to drive actions. The interaction is not blocked by any locking mechanism in either profile, so conflict risk exists in default use.
conditions: IF slim writes into a directory also used to store awesome-selfhosted-derived notes or exports
IF multiple slim runs target the same filesystem path without external locking
mitigations: Use separate output directories per run
Avoid concurrent writes to shared paths
Keep awesome-selfhosted content read-only
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared artifacts

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-selfhosted can supply tool recommendations or operational steps, and slim can execute shell commands and modify files based on operator input. If the list output is treated as authoritative, slim may carry forward incorrect or outdated guidance into destructive container actions. The pair lacks a verification step by default, so errors can cascade into real changes.
conditions: IF an operator uses awesome-selfhosted entries as authoritative instructions for slim
IF slim executes commands derived from those entries without independent verification
mitigations: Verify recommendations against primary docs before execution
Require a human approval step for shell commands
Limit slim to dry-run mode where possible
Record source links alongside copied guidance
requires-engineering: add validation checks before command execution

E_compliance.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a public knowledge list with no sensitive data classes, while slim handles certificate private keys, registry credentials, and environment variables. If those sensitive artifacts are processed in the same workflow, compliance obligations around secrets handling and retention can be violated. The other agent is not cited for residency because no residency data is present.
conditions: IF slim processes certificate private keys or registry credentials in a shared workflow
IF logs or exports from slim are retained alongside public awesome-selfhosted notes
mitigations: Exclude secrets from shared notes and exports
Minimize retention of slim logs
Store credentials outside the analysis workspace
Review whether any sensitive artifacts are being copied into public documentation
requires-engineering: implement secret-redaction and retention controls
